name: App actions for assistants (App Intents, AppFunctions)
plain: Lets Siri, Shortcuts or Gemini run actions inside an app.
meaning: An app exposes verbs and data to the system assistant, so a voice request can act without opening the app. Modern assistants can chain these across apps.

android.permission: None; AppFunctions via androidx.appfunctions (experimental), shortcuts.xml capabilities for older App Actions
android.prompt_ui: Assistant asks before sensitive actions; app function access limited to trusted agents
android.api_surface: androidx.appfunctions, Google Assistant App Actions (built-in intents), Shortcuts API
android.note: AppFunctions is the Android 16 analogue of App Intents; limited to privileged assistant callers.

ios.prompt_ui: Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight and Action button show intents; confirmation dialogs set by developer
ios.note: iOS 18 and 26 let Siri and Apple Intelligence chain and understand app content with App Intents.

limits.headline: Can let Siri, Shortcuts or Gemini run actions inside the app, with your confirmation
limits.user_action: You ask Siri or Gemini to do something, or tap an action in Shortcuts or Spotlight
can: Run an action in the app by voice or a shortcut
Show actions in Spotlight and on the Action button on iPhone
Chain actions together on iPhone with Apple Intelligence
cannot: Run sensitive actions without asking you first
Let any app call another app's actions on Android; callers are limited to privileged assistants
Take actions you have not allowed in the Siri or Shortcuts settings
limits.differs: iPhone uses App Intents. Android 16 uses AppFunctions, limited to trusted assistants.

story.what_it_is: Lets Siri, Shortcuts or Gemini do tasks inside an app without opening it.

marketing.name: App Intents
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps expose actions and content to Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight.

marketing.name: AppFunctions
marketing.pitch: Google describes AppFunctions as a way for AI assistants to call actions in apps on Android 16.

story.for_you: You say add milk to my list or play my workout playlist and it happens without opening the app. You may be asked to confirm sensitive steps.
story.for_makers: Makers get their features inside assistants and search. Modern assistants can chain actions across apps, which raises the risk of tricks hidden in content an assistant reads.

use_cases.example: You ask Siri to add a task and it appears in your to do app.
You say play my morning mix and Spotify starts.
You ask to reorder your usual coffee from a voice command.
You start a workout from the Action button.
You tell the assistant to lock the door through your home app.
A voice command opens a game level or starts a daily challenge.
You ask for a ride home without opening the app.

story.android_note: AppFunctions arrive with Android 16 and work only with trusted assistants.
story.ios_note: iOS 18 and 26 let Siri and Apple Intelligence chain and understand app content.

technical_bounds: Android AppFunctions callers are restricted; adoption limited

history.change: App Intents replaces most SiriKit use
Intents across Spotlight, Visual Intelligence and Apple Intelligence
